corrections.originalCritique: Strongest feature: The reply perceptively relocates the dependence problem from separately existing parts to the unifying fact that makes a plurality constitute one God, directly contacting the critic's proposal that the whole might ground its own components. Principal limitation: The argument presupposes that unity must be an explanatory factor distinguishable from the whole, whereas an opponent could identify unity with the whole's primitive nature or treat internal differentiation as noncompositional and therefore requiring no additional unifier. Live burden: The defender must show that every genuine intrinsic plurality entails a unifying ground explanatory of the whole, then explain why God cannot primitively or reflexively ground that unity without vicious circularity. Locked score: The supplied very-strong placement appropriately rewards focused responsiveness, conceptual precision, calibrated phrasing, and substantial dialectical progress, while leaving the ontology of unity incompletely defended.
